prompt: A team spreads three virtual machines over zones 1, 2 and 3 of `brazilsouth` in one subscription. What have they bought?
hint: Inside one subscription, is the numbering stable?

choices.text: Protection against losing the whole region
choices.why: Three zones are still one region. Losing the region loses all three.

choices.text: Survival of the loss of any one zone
choices.why: Right. Inside one subscription, 1, 2 and 3 are three different physical zones.

choices.text: Nothing, since logical zones are random per machine
choices.why: The mapping is per subscription and stable inside it, not per machine.

choices.text: A second copy of each disk in the paired region
choices.why: Zones are inside the region; the pair is a different subject.

prompt: A command copied from a forum returns `Please run 'az login' to setup account.` in the course's lab. What has been sent to Azure?
hint: Where does that message come from?

choices.text: Nothing at all
choices.why: Right. The CLI found no sign-in in its own memory and stopped.

choices.text: A request that Resource Manager refused
choices.why: Resource Manager never saw it. The refusal is the CLI's.

choices.text: A sign-in attempt that Entra ID rejected
choices.why: No sign-in was attempted; that would need `az login`.

choices.text: A telemetry record of the command
choices.why: `env.sh` turns telemetry off with `AZURE_CORE_COLLECT_TELEMETRY=no`.

prompt: Which pairing is drawn in the lesson as running one way only?

choices.text: `southcentralus` with `northcentralus`
choices.why: Those two are each other's pair.

choices.text: `brazilsouth` with `brazilsoutheast`
choices.why: Brazil South's pair is not Brazil Southeast; the arrow runs the other way.

choices.text: None: every Azure pair is mutual
choices.why: Two of the drawn pairs are one-way.

choices.text: `brazilsouth` with `southcentralus`
choices.why: Right. South Central US's own pair is North Central US.

prompt: Order the setup of the lab as lesson 1 does it.
hint: The CLI needs its environment before Bicep can be fetched through it.
items: install the Ubuntu packages with apt
create the virtual environment and install the Azure CLI
fetch the Bicep CLI with az bicep install
trap: Bicep comes last: it is fetched by the CLI, and the CLI is on the path only after env.sh is read.

prompt: Which of these does a region's pair decide for you? Choose all that apply.
hint: Microsoft chooses the pair, not you.

choices.text: Where geo-redundant storage keeps its second copy
choices.why: Right, and you do not choose it.

choices.text: Which of the two regions gets a platform update first
choices.why: Right. Updates roll out one region of a pair at a time.

choices.text: Where your virtual machines restart after an outage
choices.why: Nothing moves them for you; recovery is a design you build.

choices.text: The price of data moved between the two regions
choices.why: Data between regions is billed per gigabyte, paired or not.

prompt: In which box do the shop's users live?

choices.text: The management group `mg-shop`
choices.why: Management groups hold subscriptions.

choices.text: The subscription `shop-prod`
choices.why: A subscription holds resources and the bill, not users.

choices.text: The tenant
choices.why: Right. The subscription trusts it for identities.

choices.text: A resource group named after the team
choices.why: An identity is not a resource in a group.

prompt: Which part of `/subscriptions/bbbbcccc-1111-dddd-2222-eeee3333ffff/resourceGroups/rg-shop-prod/providers/Microsoft.Network/virtualNetworks/vnet-shop-prod` says who pays for the network?

choices.text: `rg-shop-prod`
choices.why: The group sorts; the subscription pays.

choices.text: `Microsoft.Network`
choices.why: That is the provider that owns the type.

choices.text: `vnet-shop-prod`
choices.why: That is the name of what is being paid for.

choices.text: `bbbbcccc-1111-dddd-2222-eeee3333ffff`
choices.why: Right. The subscription is the box of money.

prompt: Match each Bicep `targetScope` to the `$schema` its compiled template carries.
hint: The schema is named after the scope.

prompt: Two scripts store the same network's id, one as `.../resourceGroups/rg-shop-prod/...` and one as `.../resourcegroups/RG-SHOP-PROD/...`. Which statement is true?

choices.text: Azure treats them as two networks
choices.why: Resource Manager compares ids without regard to case.

choices.text: The second id is refused by every Azure tool
choices.why: Azure accepts it; it is the same resource.

choices.text: Azure sees one network; a plain `==` sees two
choices.why: Right. Lower-case ids before comparing them.

choices.text: Both scripts will agree, since strings ignore case
choices.why: A plain string comparison is case-sensitive.

prompt: Which of these are true of a resource group? Choose all that apply.
hint: Think of what the group decides and what it does not.

choices.text: It belongs to exactly one subscription
choices.why: Right. It is a box inside one subscription.

choices.text: Its resources must be in its own region
choices.why: Its location is only where its record is kept.

choices.text: Deleting it deletes everything inside it
choices.why: Right, which makes it the unit of cleaning up.

choices.text: It may contain other resource groups
choices.why: Resource groups do not nest.

prompt: A virtual network is moved from one resource group to another in the same subscription. Which of these keeps working without anybody touching it?
hint: A move renames; it does not relocate.

choices.text: A script that looks the network up by its old resource id
choices.why: The id changed, so the script now asks for something that does not exist.

choices.text: The machines connected to it
choices.why: Right. Traffic is untouched; only the name moved.

choices.text: A role assignment made directly on the network
choices.why: It is left behind as an orphan.

choices.text: An alert rule that names the network's old id
choices.why: Anything holding the old id points at nothing after the move.

prompt: A team must take an Azure Firewall from `rg-shop-prod` into `rg-shop-platform`. What does the move table imply they plan for?
hint: The firewall's row says No twice.

choices.text: A new firewall in the destination and a cut-over window
choices.why: Right. A type that cannot move is recreated and switched over.

choices.text: A validation first, then `az resource move`
choices.why: The validation would refuse it for the type.

choices.text: A move with both groups locked for a few hours
choices.why: There is no move: the type cannot move at all.

choices.text: A support request so that Microsoft moves it for them
choices.why: Support cannot move what the platform does not move.

prompt: Order the three steps Microsoft describes for moving a resource and its dependencies to another subscription.
items: gather the dependencies into one resource group
move that group's resources in one request
spread them into groups again at the destination
trap: Spreading is optional; gathering is not.

prompt: Which operation deletes every role assignment in a subscription, by Microsoft's documentation?

choices.text: Moving the subscription to another management group
choices.why: That changes what is inherited, and deletes nothing.

choices.text: Moving all its resources into one resource group
choices.why: Only assignments on the moved resources themselves are orphaned.

choices.text: Registering a new resource provider in it
choices.why: Registration touches no permission.

choices.text: Transferring it to a different tenant
choices.why: Right. The assignments named identities of the old tenant.

prompt: Which question does Azure Policy answer, as distinct from role-based access control?
hint: One is about the identity, the other about the resource.

choices.text: May this identity make this request?
choices.why: That is role-based access.

choices.text: May the resource this request describes exist here?
choices.why: Right. Whoever asks.

choices.text: Which tenant does this identity belong to?
choices.why: That is Entra ID's question.

choices.text: How much will this resource cost?
choices.why: Cost is lessons 13 to 15.

prompt: *Allowed locations* is assigned on `mg-shop` in mode `Indexed`. Somebody creates a resource group in Texas under it. What happens?
hint: What does the definition's description exclude?

choices.text: It is refused
choices.why: `Indexed` does not look at resource groups.

choices.text: It is created in `brazilsouth` instead
choices.why: Policy never relocates a request.

choices.text: It is created; that definition does not look at groups
choices.why: Right. *Allowed locations for resource groups*, in mode `All`, is the one that would.

choices.text: It is created and its resources are refused forever
choices.why: Resources in it are judged by their own locations.

prompt: Order these effects as Azure Policy runs them on a request.
hint: Switch-off first, change before refuse, refuse before report.
trap: `append` shares its place with `modify`: both can change the request.

prompt: Which way out of an inherited policy is visible, written down, and ends on a date?
hint: It has categories: waiver and mitigated.

choices.text: A policy exemption
choices.why: Right. For one scope, from one assignment, until `expiresOn`.

choices.text: `DoNotEnforce` on the assignment
choices.why: That loosens it for everybody under it, with no date.

choices.text: Assigning the definition again below with `disabled`
choices.why: That does not switch off the assignment above.

choices.text: Moving the subscription to the root group
choices.why: That changes inheritance for everything in it and is not written as an exception.

prompt: In the Cloud Adoption Framework's tree, where do a workload's production and staging subscriptions go?
hint: Environments are not a reason for a management group.

choices.text: In two management groups, one per environment
choices.why: CAF advises against that split.

choices.text: Directly under the tenant root group
choices.why: Nothing of the organisation's should hang there.

choices.text: Production under platform, staging under sandbox
choices.why: Platform is for the platform team's own subscriptions.

choices.text: Side by side in the same landing zone group
choices.why: Right. Same rules, so a test means something.

prompt: Why can a deployment stack not manage the management group tree itself?
hint: At which scopes do stacks exist?

choices.text: Management groups cannot be described in Bicep
choices.why: They can; lesson 5 compiled a tree.

choices.text: Management groups are tenant-level resources, and there are no stacks at the tenant
choices.why: Right. Stacks exist at resource group, subscription and management group scope.

choices.text: Stacks only manage virtual machines and networks
choices.why: Stacks manage any resource at their scope.

choices.text: A stack would lock the tenant root group
choices.why: No stack can be created there in the first place.

prompt: Match each date to what stops in the retirement of Azure Blueprints.
What does subscription vending give a workload team?
hint: Compare with a subscription made by hand.

choices.text: A subscription that arrives placed, budgeted and connected
choices.why: Right. Nobody creates one by hand.

choices.text: A discount on the subscription's first year
choices.why: Vending is about governance, not price.

choices.text: A copy of the platform landing zone of its own
choices.why: The platform is built once for everybody.

choices.text: A subscription with Owner on the whole management group tree
choices.why: CAF advises against roles for workload teams at management group scope.

prompt: A company wants its helpdesk in Recife to reset passwords for the Recife office only. What does Entra ID offer for that?
hint: The scope of a directory role.

choices.text: A management group for Recife, with the role given there
choices.why: Management groups divide Azure resources, not the directory.

choices.text: A dynamic group whose rule names Recife
choices.why: A group collects members; it does not limit what an administrator reaches.

choices.text: An administrative unit, with User Administrator scoped to it
choices.why: Right. The role then reaches the unit's members only.

choices.text: A second tenant for the Recife office
choices.why: That splits the company's identities in two, which nobody asked for.

prompt: Which identifier should a log keep to say which person did something, in a way that survives a change of name?
hint: One of a user's names never changes.

choices.text: The user principal name
choices.why: It changes when a person or a domain is renamed.

choices.text: The display name
choices.why: It is the least stable of all, and not unique.

choices.text: The e-mail address
choices.why: A user need not have one, and it changes like the name.

choices.text: The object id
choices.why: Right. A GUID Entra ID assigns once.

prompt: An Owner of every subscription asks to reset a colleague's password, and is refused. Which statement explains it?

choices.text: The colleague is in a restricted administrative unit
choices.why: Possible in general, but an Owner is refused for any user.

choices.text: Owners need to elevate access first
choices.why: Elevation goes the other way: from Global Administrator to Azure resources.

choices.text: Azure roles grant nothing in the directory
choices.why: Right. Passwords are the directory's, and need a directory role.

choices.text: Password resets need a second factor the Owner lacks
choices.why: The refusal is about the role, not the factor.

prompt: A person from another organisation invited into the tenant is a ___ user.
A deployment pipeline outside Azure needs to reach Resource Manager. Which credential leaves nothing in the pipeline that could leak?

choices.text: A federated credential, exchanging the CI system's own tokens
choices.why: Right. The pipeline's issuer vouches for the job, and nothing is stored.

choices.text: A certificate in the pipeline's secret store
choices.why: The private key is still stored there.

choices.text: A client secret renewed every 90 days
choices.why: Shorter, but still a stored string.

choices.text: The tenant id and subscription id
choices.why: Neither is a credential at all.

prompt: Which object receives an Azure role when a program is given access?
hint: The one that signs in, in that tenant.

choices.text: The application registration
choices.why: The registration defines the program; it is not what signs in.

choices.text: The service principal
choices.why: Right, by its object id.

choices.text: The client secret
choices.why: A secret is a proof, not a principal.

choices.text: The application (client) id
choices.why: That id names the program everywhere and no object here.

prompt: A federated credential's subject is widened from one branch to `repo:shop-example/storefront:*`-style matching of every ref. What risk does that create?
hint: Who runs workflows on other refs?

choices.text: Tokens will last longer than an hour
choices.why: Lifetime does not depend on the subject.

choices.text: GitHub will stop signing the tokens
choices.why: GitHub signs every job's token regardless.

choices.text: Entra ID will refuse every exchange
choices.why: A wider subject accepts more, not less.

choices.text: Every branch's workflow gets the deploy identity
choices.why: Right. The subject is where the security is.

prompt: A program with no person behind it signs in with the client ___ flow.
Ten web apps must all read one storage account, and are rebuilt often. Which identity arrangement keeps the role list shortest and survives rebuilds?

choices.text: A system-assigned identity on each app
choices.why: Ten principals, and each rebuild loses its role.

choices.text: A service principal with a secret in each app's settings
choices.why: That stores ten copies of a secret.

choices.text: One user-assigned identity shared by all ten
choices.why: Right. One role assignment, kept across rebuilds.

choices.text: The subscription's own identity
choices.why: A subscription has no identity of that kind.

prompt: A program on an Azure VM with a managed identity also finds `AZURE_TENANT_ID`, `AZURE_CLIENT_ID` and `AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET` in its environment. Which identity does `DefaultAzureCredential` use?

choices.text: The managed identity, because it is on Azure
choices.why: It comes third; the environment is tried first.

choices.text: The service principal in the environment variables
choices.why: Right. `EnvironmentCredential` is first, and stops the chain even if it fails.

choices.text: Whichever has more roles
choices.why: The class never compares roles.

choices.text: Neither: two configured credentials is an error
choices.why: No such check exists.

prompt: Why does code on a VM need no credential to get its managed identity's token?

choices.text: The platform signs in, and hands back a token at a local address
choices.why: Right. The metadata service answers only that machine.

choices.text: The VM's disk holds a certificate Azure rotates
choices.why: Nothing is on the disk.

choices.text: Entra ID trusts every request from Azure's IP ranges
choices.why: Addresses are never trusted in this flow.

choices.text: The token is created when the VM is deployed and never expires
choices.why: Tokens expire, and the platform renews them.

prompt: The Instance Metadata Service answers at the link-local address `169.254.169.___`.
A user holds Reader on the subscription and Contributor on one resource group in it. What may they do in that resource group?

choices.text: Everything Contributor allows
choices.why: Right. Reader adds nothing to Contributor there.

choices.text: Only read, because the wider scope wins
choices.why: Scopes do not compete; every assignment that covers the resource counts.

choices.text: Only read, because Reader's notActions remove writing
choices.why: Reader has no notActions; it simply allows `*/read`.

choices.text: Nothing, because two assignments on one person conflict
choices.why: They do not conflict; they add up.

prompt: Which of these takes a permission away from a person whatever their other roles allow?

choices.text: A `notActions` entry in one of their roles
choices.why: It narrows that role only.

choices.text: Removing them from Reader on the subscription
choices.why: Another assignment may still allow it.

choices.text: An empty `dataActions` in a custom role
choices.why: Empty means the role grants no data operations, not that it forbids them.

choices.text: A deny assignment covering the resource
choices.why: Right. It is checked first and beats every allow.

prompt: Reader's whole definition is one action: `*/___`.
hint: Every operation whose name ends in it.

prompt: Why should a role assignment's name in Bicep be `guid()` of the scope, the principal and the role?

choices.text: Because the portal sorts assignments by name
choices.why: Sorting is not the reason.

choices.text: So a repeated deployment finds the same assignment
choices.why: Right. The same inputs give the same GUID.

choices.text: So that every deployment creates a new, unique assignment
choices.why: The point is the opposite: the same assignment every time.

choices.text: Because Bicep refuses any other name
choices.why: The compiler accepts any name.

prompt: In Privileged Identity Management, what does an eligible assignment give before it is activated?

choices.why: That would be an active assignment.

choices.text: Read access, with writes after activation
choices.why: It gives no part of the role before activation.

choices.text: The right to ask for the role

choices.text: The role for the first 24 hours
choices.why: Nothing is held until somebody activates.

prompt: What is the range Microsoft documents for an activation's maximum duration?

choices.text: 1 to 8 hours
choices.why: The upper bound is higher.

choices.text: 1 to 7 days
choices.why: Activations are measured in hours.

choices.text: 1 to 24 hours
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: Any length, if approved
choices.why: Approval does not lift the maximum.

prompt: A Global Administrator elevated themselves to manage every subscription last month and forgot it. What does that person hold now?

choices.why: Right. Every subscription, and the power to grant any role.

choices.text: Nothing: the switch turns itself off after a day
choices.why: It stays on until somebody switches it off.

choices.text: Reader on every subscription

choices.text: An eligible Owner assignment on each subscription

prompt: Order the kinds of access from the most standing to the least.

choices.text: The sign-in is blocked
choices.why: Right. Any applicable block wins.

choices.text: The older policy decides

choices.text: The person chooses which policy to satisfy

choices.text: Users running Terraform from a laptop

choices.text: Service principals and managed identities

prompt: In which year did Microsoft begin enforcing MFA for sign-ins to the Azure portal?

choices.text: Blocked all sign-ins until a policy is written

prompt: Which sign-in method lets people sign in to Azure while the office's servers are all down?
